introCutscene.text: A video of Mayor Chen just went viral. In it, she looks directly at the camera and says: 'I can no longer serve this city. I resign effective immediately.'
Mayor Chen has served Veritas for 12 years. She’s never missed a vote or a public appearance. Her integrity is what got her elected.
Her office says she was attending a charity dinner at the time this video was created. But the file was uploaded at 2:47 AM — three hours before that dinner started.
The opposition is calling for an emergency election. News outlets are running the story. The city is in chaos.
GIHA intercepted this file before it spread to every screen in Veritas. Your job: determine if this video is authentic or fabricated.
Check the audio spectrogram for synthetic markers. Step through each frame. Look for anything that doesn't belong.

evidenceFindings.evidence-01: The video is 30 seconds long, 1080p. The mayor's mouth movements look slightly off — a frame-by-frame advance reveals micro-mismatches between audio and lip shapes.
evidenceFindings.evidence-02: The audio spectrogram shows a clean voice profile but the high-frequency range (2-4kHz) has an unusual pattern — consistent with AI voice synthesis, not natural human speech.
evidenceFindings.evidence-03: File metadata shows the video was created in Vegas Pro at 2:47 AM — three hours before the mayor's official alibi places her at a charity dinner. Creation software matches known deepfake toolchains.
evidenceFindings.evidence-04: Social media comments are split: half demanding resignation, half claiming the video is fake. Several accounts pushing the resignation narrative were created in the last 48 hours — a common astroturfing tactic. Note: these comments reveal the motive behind the campaign, not the video’s origin. Analyze the video file itself first.
evidenceFindings.evidence-05: Side-by-side comparison with an official video of Mayor Chen shows her natural speaking style includes hand gestures and pauses. The viral video lacks these — it's a static headshot with animated mouth movement.
evidenceFindings.evidence-06: Upload server logs reveal the video was posted via a VPN registered to VeraTech Solutions — a shell company controlled by a network calling itself The Shadow Collective. The IP traces to a data center used exclusively by known disinformation operators. The same shell company later funded the Harborview voice scam operation (Case 2), using the same numbered account structure.

toolHints.spectrogram: Best tool for this case. Visualizes audio frequency spectrum. AI-generated speech often leaves distinctive artifacts in the 2-4kHz range.
toolHints.frame-stepper: Essential for video analysis. Best tool for this case. Advances video one frame at a time to spot mismatches between audio waveforms and lip movements.
toolHints.metadata-inspector: Extracts file headers, creation timestamps, and editing history. Reveals Vegas Pro origin and conflict with mayor's alibi.
toolHints.source-tracer: Simulates reverse image search. Shows earliest known publication date and matching sources across the web.
toolHints.inconsistency-highlighter: Detects lighting, shadow, and perspective anomalies. Helps identify composited or AI-generated visual elements.
toolHints.timeline-cross-referencer: Places all evidence on a chronological timeline. Highlights impossible sequences or conflicting timestamps.

conclusionText: The video was a deepfake. An AI-generated audio track was overlaid onto footage of Mayor Chen's public address — the voice model was trained on clips from her public speeches using a generative adversarial network. The 2-4kHz audio artifact is a signature of current-generation voice synthesis models. The creator used Vegas Pro — a common deepfake production tool — and uploaded the file through an anonymous VPN registered to VeraTech Solutions, a shell company controlled by the Shadow Collective. In 2026, deepfake detection requires examining multiple modalities: audio, visual, and metadata. One clue alone isn't enough — but together, they reveal the truth.
milLesson: Deepfakes target multiple senses simultaneously. Always verify through audio analysis, frame inspection, and source checking — no single test is sufficient.
